title: Bridging Speed and Optimality in Job Scheduling: A Hybrid Ant Colony Optimization Approach for Distributed Systems
problem: Job scheduling in distributed systems suffers from exponential complexity; trade-off between speed (heuristics) and optimality (solvers) is fundamental
motivation: Bridge the speed-optimality gap for scalable job scheduling in distributed systems
method: Hybrid Ant Colony Optimization with queue-based warm-start, disjunctive graphs for constraints, parallel local search on subgraphs, OR-Tools integration
key_novelty: HACO algorithm combining heuristic speed with optimization-grade quality; demonstrates 5-10x speedup with only 3-5% suboptimality
contributions: HACO algorithm design with strategic pheromone initialization and local search
Disjunctive graph formulation for precedence and resource constraints
Evaluation on JSSP, FJSP, and synthetic large-scale problems showing scalability
limitations: Evaluation limited to synthetic problems; real-world distributed system workload characteristics not extensively explored
primary_theme: Hybrid optimization for scalable distributed scheduling
